items.passage: Male tree crickets (Oecanthus henryi) can extend the range of their mating calls by chewing a hole in a leaf and calling through it, an acoustic amplification technique known as baffling. Most males are physically capable of ______ a 2020 study found that the strategy is used predominantly by smaller, quieter individuals.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: “Most males are physically capable of baffling” and “a 2020 study found that the strategy is used predominantly by smaller, quieter individuals” are both independent clauses. Two independent clauses can be joined by a comma followed by a coordinating conjunction, so “baffling, but” is correct.

A.why_wrong: “But” joins two independent clauses here, and a comma must come before it.

C.why_wrong: A comma alone cannot join the two independent clauses.

D.why_wrong: No comma belongs after “but”; it wrongly separates the conjunction from the clause it introduces.

B.why_wrong: “And” joins two independent clauses here, so a comma is needed before it.

C.why_wrong: A comma alone cannot join the two independent clauses.

D.why_wrong: With no punctuation and no conjunction, the two independent clauses run together.

A.why_wrong: With no mark or conjunction, the introductory phrase runs straight on from “audience,” and the two independent clauses are fused.

items.passage: Analyzing 174 conversations she had recorded in 1974 among Ju/’hoan foragers in northwestern Botswana, anthropologist Polly Wiessner showed in 2014 that daytime talk centered largely on economic matters and on complaints and criticism of other people’s ______ 81 percent of the long nighttime conversations that involved many people were devoted to telling stories.

A.why_wrong: Placing the semicolon after “by contrast” attaches the phrase to the description of daytime talk, which contrasts with nothing before it.

C.why_wrong: Commas around “by contrast” leave the two independent clauses joined by a comma alone.

items.passage: In a 2015 survey of more than 3,700 languages, a team led by linguist Caleb Everett found that complex tone, in which several pitch patterns distinguish words, has rarely developed in very cold or arid climates. Such a correlation could be ______ the researchers link it to laryngological evidence that inhaling dry air makes vocal fold vibration less precise.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
items.explanation: “Such a correlation could be coincidental, though” concedes a limitation of the finding described in the first sentence, so “though” belongs at the end of this first independent clause, set off by a comma. A semicolon then joins it to the second independent clause, “the researchers link it to laryngological evidence ....”

B.why_wrong: With commas on both sides of “though,” the two independent clauses are joined by a comma alone.

C.why_wrong: After a semicolon, “though” acts as a subordinating conjunction, so “though the researchers link it to ...” is a dependent clause that cannot stand after a semicolon.

D.why_wrong: The comma after “though” is the only mark between the two independent clauses, so they are spliced.

How ______ In 2020, a team led by Casey Honniball used the airborne telescope SOFIA to detect light at a wavelength unique to water molecules.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: researchers could tell the two apart?
could researchers tell the two apart?
could researchers tell the two apart.
researchers could tell the two apart.
items.explanation: “How ...” begins a direct question that stands as its own sentence, so the helping verb must come before the subject (“could researchers”) and the sentence must end with a question mark.

A.recipe: question errors: direct question left uninverted
A.why_wrong: A direct question needs the helping verb before the subject; “How researchers could tell the two apart?” keeps statement word order.

C.recipe: question errors: question ending in a period
C.why_wrong: The inverted wording makes this a direct question, so it must end with a question mark, not a period.

D.recipe: question errors: statement order with a period
D.why_wrong: “How researchers could tell the two apart.” is not a complete sentence; a stand-alone question needs inverted order and a question mark.

sources.what: NASA: earlier observations detected hydration but could not tell water from hydroxyl; SOFIA detected the 6.1-micron wavelength specific to water molecules in Clavius crater; lead author Casey Honniball; published October 26, 2020
Honniball et al. 2020, Nature Astronomy, “Molecular water detected on the sunlit Moon by SOFIA”
